transcript.text: Alright, let's get started. We need to finalize the managed event-streaming service decision for the audit-event pipeline so we're ready for production integration next month. The current draft recommends NimbusMQ based on the lower initial quote and our existing SDK integration, and staging showed both NimbusMQ and StreamForge handling 20,000 events per second without errors. Before I make the binding decision, I want to hear from backend engineering and procurement. Who wants to kick things off?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something critical before we go further. This morning, while helping another team investigate a load-test harness, I confirmed that the production burst requirement for the audit-event pipeline is 35,000 events per second. NimbusMQ throttles at 25,000 events per second, while StreamForge supports up to 40,000. I haven't updated the architecture document yet because the harness investigation was a separate task, but this directly impacts our service selection — NimbusMQ would not meet the production burst requirement.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical procurement issue. I received the latest data-processing terms from our legal review just an hour ago. Because the audit pipeline will process events from EU customers, EU customer audit events must be stored in an EU region. Between our two shortlisted services, only StreamForge offers the required EU region under the shortlisted contracts. NimbusMQ does not. I have not yet attached these terms to the architecture review, but this data-residency requirement means NimbusMQ would not be compliant for our EU customer data.
